mbm-0343.clue: I went to see the enormous whale.
mbm-0343.quote: I stayed for the brass hinge on the model whaler’s door. Someone had filed it by hand and fitted it with four little screws. That’s the part I drew on the train home.

mbm-0344.clue: I know who gets the middle cushion.
mbm-0344.quote: At our pajama cartoon nights the middle cushion goes to whoever sings the opening theme in the strangest voice. My aunt won with an opera version. She nearly brought down the lampshade on the high note.

mbm-0345.clue: I borrowed a mirror halfway through this quilt.
mbm-0345.quote: I took half a spiral to my barber and laid it against his big tilting mirror. One patch stood out like a crooked tooth. He turned the chair around so I could unpick it in the good light.

mbm-0346.clue: I can make a spoon appear in a very strange place.
mbm-0346.quote: I hid the silver spoon in my cuff for a dinner-table trick. My nephew set down an extra soup bowl to catch it. The spoon landed neatly inside, and for once we both looked like experts.

mbm-0347.clue: My beach bag has a weather vane.
mbm-0347.quote: I tied a strip of pink cloth to the volleyball net before a windy match. Nobody agreed which way to serve until we looked up. Now the pink strip gets called captain.

mbm-0348.clue: I save the last slice for the landing.
mbm-0348.quote: Dad and I carry one apple on our canoe trip, cutting slices when we stop to drift. The last piece always waits until the canoe nose touches the gravel, no matter how slowly we’ve paddled.

mbm-0349.clue: My game begins before anyone rolls.
mbm-0349.quote: I made little cloth bags for our board-game pieces. Everybody picks a bag by feel. I always hope for the lumpy one because the old wooden ferry fits only in that one.

mbm-0350.clue: I sing above the rattling bottles.
mbm-0350.quote: Our milkman used to hum on the morning round. I sang the high part from the porch. When he retired, the neighbors rolled out a whole crate of empty bottles and tapped us one last accompaniment.

mbm-0351.clue: I keep a plum in my pocket for the finale.
mbm-0351.quote: After three cups and a bead, I lift the final cup and show a plum. Last week I forgot to bring it and used my mother’s tomato. The front row asked for the recipe.

mbm-0352.clue: I count by the colors of the plates.
mbm-0352.quote: I learned to load the weights at a gym with a bright coat of paint on every plate. My little brother drew my best lift as red, blue, blue. I knew exactly what he meant.

mbm-0353.clue: I have the beach chair with the little window.
mbm-0353.quote: I repaired a torn canvas back with an open square of net. When I stretch out in the sun I can see one very small piece of sea through it. My nephew thinks it’s a submarine periscope.

mbm-0354.clue: My teammate has a whistle with feathers.
mbm-0354.quote: At our beach volleyball court a gull kept crying just after every point. We followed its calls for an entire set until it flew off halfway through a rally. Best referee we’d had all summer.

mbm-0355.clue: I follow the bell to the top.
mbm-0355.quote: There’s a little wooden gate just below the summit and the farmer tied a bell to it. On a misty hike I heard my friend ring it ahead of me. The hill felt a great deal smaller after that.

mbm-0356.clue: My rook has a little garden.
mbm-0356.quote: The old park rook is hollow underneath. A child tucked a daisy inside after our match, so when I lifted it the rook stood over a white flower. I let the next player discover it.

mbm-0357.clue: I always let the elephant choose first.
mbm-0357.quote: Our game box has a mismatched elephant token from a different game. We point its trunk at the starting player. I’m convinced it points toward whoever has brought the best biscuits.

mbm-0358.clue: I stitched a wave into every corner.
mbm-0358.quote: I made our picnic quilt from the shirts we wore at the lake. Four little waves point toward the middle. When we spread it out, the sandwiches go on the only dry island.

mbm-0359.clue: I learned the tune by watching the curtains.
mbm-0359.quote: My neighbor practices vallenato behind thin curtains. I watched the bellows opening and closing in silhouette and tried the rhythm on my own accordion. One evening he threw open the yellow shutters and taught me the rest.

mbm-0360.clue: My camera wore a shower cap.
mbm-0360.quote: We wrapped the camera in a pink shower cap for our rafting trip. When we took the cap off at the landing, I put it on over my helmet for the crew portrait. It’s my mother’s favorite picture.

mbm-0361.clue: I retired my first dragon to the windowsill.
mbm-0361.quote: The purple ink bleached away on my favorite fantasy card. Now the dragon is a silvery ghost. I gave it a tiny frame and bring it to the table to watch the new deck play.

mbm-0362.clue: I only noticed the tiny handprint on the way down.
mbm-0362.quote: On our climbing wall my niece left a little chalky handprint below the first hold. I climbed the whole route and missed it. Back on the floor it looked like the most important move of the day.

mbm-0363.clue: My best hat has a tail.
mbm-0363.quote: I crocheted a pointed hat for my cousin, who asked for a comet. I made the yellow tail too long and it trailed over his shoulder. He insists that’s how you know the comet is moving.

mbm-0364.clue: I give my stories a front-door key.
mbm-0364.quote: I hang an old brass key above my writing desk. Before I begin a new town I decide which door it opens. This time it’s a station cupboard where somebody has been leaving fresh oranges.

mbm-0365.clue: I plan the halftime snack before the film.
mbm-0365.quote: Our old family comedy breaks for commercials at exactly the moment the pies fly. I put toast in the toaster at the first airborne pie. My friends call me the official pajama projectionist.

mbm-0366.clue: I used my little sister’s short pencil.
mbm-0366.quote: She keeps my golf scores with a yellow pencil sharpened to the length of a tee. At the ninth green I offered to swap it for a new one. She asked what we’d do for luck on the back nine.

mbm-0367.clue: I saved the ribbon with the red drip.
mbm-0367.quote: The watermelon contest ended with red juice on my wrist and a white participation ribbon. I wiped my nose with the wrong hand, so there’s a streak of real juice beside the printed slice. I couldn’t have designed it better.
